content: I'll start by reading the test image and the part index simultaneously.

**Test image analysis:** The image shows the crown/base area of sugarcane plants. The central leaf has a distinctly **yellow midrib** running down it, with otherwise green leaf tissue. Some older/outer leaves appear yellowish and drying. This yellow midrib is a key diagnostic feature.

The plant part is **leaf/whole plant**. Candidates from the part index: Brown_Spot, Leaf_Scald, Pokkah_Boeng, Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv, Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus, Yellow_Leaf, Yellow_Spot, Grassy_Shoot.

The yellow midrib strongly suggests **Yellow_Leaf**. Now I'll check one reference from 4 different classes.

Yellow_Leaf reference shows golden/yellow discoloration across the leaf - matches the advanced stage. The test image shows an earlier stage with yellow midrib on still-green leaf. Now checking Leaf_Scald.
Leaf_Scald shows a narrow white "pencil line" - doesn't match the test image's broader yellow midrib. Now checking Pokkah_Boeng.
Pokkah_Boeng shows twisted/malformed leaves with knife-cut patterns - doesn't match. Now checking Yellow_Spot for my 4th class.

Yellow_Spot shows scattered small yellow flecks/spots across the leaf surface - completely different from the test image.

**Final analysis:**

| Feature | Test Image | Match |
|---|---|---|
| Yellow midrib on central young leaf | ✓ prominent | Yellow_Leaf ✓ |
| Green lamina flanking the midrib | ✓ | Yellow_Leaf early stage ✓ |
| Older leaves yellowing/drying | ✓ | Yellow_Leaf (matured leaves) ✓ |
| Scattered spots | ✗ | Rules out Brown_Spot, Yellow_Spot |
| White pencil line | ✗ | Rules out Leaf_Scald |
| Twisted/deformed leaves | ✗ | Rules out Pokkah_Boeng |
| Streaks/mosaic patterns | ✗ | Rules out Streak_Mosaic, Mosaic_Virus |

The **yellow midrib** on the young central leaf is the textbook hallmark of Yellow Leaf Disease. The symptom description explicitly states: "young leaves show bright midrib yellowing while matured leaves show extensive discoloration" — exactly what is visible here.
